subject: maths
question: A man travelled four equal distances of 10 km at the speeds of 7 km/hr, 14 km/hr, 21 km/hr and 28 km/hr respectively. What is his average speed?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance for each part = 10 km

Speed for the first part = 7 km/hr

Speed for the second part = 14 km/hr

Speed for the third part = 21 km/hr

Speed for the fourth part = 28 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total distance travelled/Total Time

**Calculation:**

Time taken for the first part = 10 / 7

Time taken for the second part = 10 / 14

Time taken for the third part = 10 / 21

Time taken for the fourth part = 10 / 28

Total Distance = 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 40 km

Total Time = (10 / 7) + (10 / 14) + (10 / 21) + (10 / 28)

Total Time = 10(1/7 + 1/14 + 1/21 + 1/28)

Total Time = 10 × ((1)/(7) + (1)/(14) + (1)/(21)+ (1)/(28))

Total Time = 10 × ((12 + 6 + 4 + 3)/(84))

Total Time = 10 × ((25)/(84))

Total Time = 250/84

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

Average Speed = 40 / (250/84)

Average Speed = 3360/250

Average Speed = 336/25 km/hr

**The average speed is 336/25 km/hr.**
